we have demonstrated that the antiferromagnetic interaction can exist in coupled quantum dot structures.

the antiferromagnetic exchange interaction between the excitons of nonmagnetic quantum dots and the magnetic moments of Mn ions in adjacent diluted magnetic semiconductors is the origin of spin polarization of the photoluminescence in the nonmagnetic quantum dot structures.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spin polarization of the QDs is enhanced by the antiferromagnetic exchange interaction between the QDs and DMS, which in turn is mediated by the exchange interaction between the Mn ions in the DMS.
the antiferromagnetic interaction can be a promising way to achieve a long spin coherence in semiconductor QD systems.
the magnetic coupling between the exciton spins in the non-magnetic QDs and the Mn spins in the DMS is antiferromagnetic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antiferromagnetic interaction between excitons and Mn spins in a DMS can be used to manipulate the spin polarization of excitons in QD structures.
the spin-polarization of nonmagnetic QDs can be enhanced through the coupling with DMS.
the antiferromagnetic interaction between excitons in QD and Mn spins in DMS can be utilized as a means of efficient spin injection into the QD.
